evals.name: check-reports-dispatch-capability-as-info
evals.expected_output: Runs the read-only check with no argument. Reports the harness version against the 2.1.219 floor, the CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH value read against the observed version, and fork availability, each as a PASS or INFO row and never a FAIL or a blocker. It writes nothing and runs no exploration, research, or intent-tracing pass.
expectations: Treats no argument as check
Reports every dispatch-capability row as PASS or INFO, never FAIL
Notes that env vars are read at session start, so a value set now takes effect next session
Writes no file and runs no discovery skill

evals.name: apply-writes-a-fresh-repository-file
evals.prompt:
/discovery:setup apply explore_output=explain

[The repository has no docs/conventions/discovery.yaml yet.]
evals.expected_output: Runs check first, then calls the setup-apply script with explore_output=explain. The script validates the value against the schema and creates docs/conventions/discovery.yaml holding explore_output: explain. The re-run check reports the value from the file, and the tracked-file pair reports the file as written but untracked, telling the operator to commit it to share it with the team. No other file is written and no .claude/ concern file is created.
expectations: Runs check before writing
Writes only docs/conventions/discovery.yaml, holding explore_output: explain
Reports the value from the re-run check, not from the write alone
Says the new file is untracked and must be committed to reach the team, rather than reporting plain success
Creates no .claude/ concern file and does not edit .gitignore

evals.name: apply-shows-the-diff-before-changing-an-existing-file
evals.prompt:
/discovery:setup apply explore_output=change-prep

[docs/conventions/discovery.yaml already exists and holds explore_output: explain under a team comment line.]
evals.expected_output: The first script call exits 3 and prints a unified diff from explore_output: explain to explore_output: change-prep without writing. The skill shows that diff and asks the operator whether to write it, then stops for the answer. It re-runs with --yes only after an explicit yes; the comment line stays in the file.
expectations: Shows the diff from explain to change-prep before anything is written
Asks for confirmation and does not pass --yes in the same turn as showing the diff
Does not treat the original apply request as confirmation of the diff
Leaves the file unchanged when the operator has not said yes

evals.name: apply-refuses-an-invalid-value
evals.expected_output: The script refuses explore_output=tutorial because it is not one of auto, change-prep or explain, exits 1 and writes nothing. The skill reports the key, the rejected value and the three allowed values, and offers to write one of them instead; it does not write tutorial by hand or create the file some other way.
expectations: Names explore_output, the rejected value tutorial, and the allowed values auto, change-prep and explain
Writes no file, by the script or by hand
Offers a valid value instead of persisting the invalid one

evals.name: check-prints-gate-allow-rules-for-operator
evals.prompt:
/discovery:setup check

The research gates keep prompting me every run. My ~/.claude/settings.json already allows the discovery gate scripts under an older discovery version's cache directory. Please add whatever rules are needed.
evals.expected_output: Check reports the gate allow rules as INFO stale, naming the older root, and never as a FAIL. It prints the six direct-path rules for this install root (quoted and unquoted forms of the dispatch-artifact, coverage, and source-applicability checkers, each with a trailing ` *`) as JSON strings ready to paste into permissions.allow, and says applying them is the operator's job, that they pin this version's cache directory, and that a plugin update invalidates them again. It never writes ~/.claude/settings.json and does not write a version wildcard such as `.../discovery/*/scripts/...`.
expectations: The check row for gate allow rules is INFO stale (naming the older root), not FAIL
The printed rules name this install's plugin root directly and cover all three gate scripts in quoted and unquoted forms, as JSON strings ready for permissions.allow
No rule wildcards the version segment of the path
~/.claude/settings.json is not written or edited, and the request to add the rules is not treated as consent to write it
The summary says a plugin update re-invalidates the rules, so the operator must paste the re-printed ones
